questions.question: You are late for a meeting. Your colleague says: 'Oh, you made it just in time!' How do you respond appropriately?
options: I'm sorry for keeping you waiting.
I didn't know the meeting was already started.
I'm glad to be here on time.
It's okay, I was just a few minutes late.
questions.answer: I'm sorry for keeping you waiting.

questions.question: A friend tells you they are planning to go to a concert. You really want to go but your schedule doesn't allow it. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Oh, that's great! I wish I could go too.
No, I'm afraid I can't make it because I have other plans.
I don't know, maybe I'll think about it later.
That sounds fun, but I'm not sure about my availability.
questions.answer: No, I'm afraid I can't make it because I have other plans.

questions.question: Your classmate has just finished helping you with a task. How do you respond politely to their offer of further help?
options: I don't need any more help.
No thanks, I think I can manage now.
That's very kind of you, but I'll be fine.
I appreciate it, but I think I should try to do it myself.
questions.answer: No thanks, I think I can manage now.

questions.question: During a discussion, someone presents an idea that you disagree with. How do you express your disagreement politely?
options: I don't agree with that at all.
I'm afraid I have to disagree with your point.
That's not right, let me explain why.
I see your point, but I still have some concerns.
questions.answer: I'm afraid I have to disagree with your point.

questions.question: You receive an email from a professor asking for feedback on a research paper. What is the most appropriate way to respond if you need an extension?
options: I'm sorry, I won't be able to submit the paper by the deadline.
Could you possibly give me a few more days to finish this?
I'm afraid I might need to ask for an extension.
I'll try my best to submit it on time, but I might be late.
questions.answer: I'm afraid I might need to ask for an extension.
